item.title: Police confirm no fatalities after officers struck by vehicle in Suva
item.description: The two police officers who were hit by a vehicle near the HFC Bank Stadium on Thursday have survived. However, we are still trying to find out the nature and severity of their injuries.
item.content:encoded:
The two police officers who were hit by a vehicle near the HFC Bank Stadium on Thursday have survived.

However, we are still trying to find out the nature and severity of their injuries.

Police say all officers involved in the incident were taken to the Colonial War Memorial Hospital for medical examinations.

A video is circulating on social media by Tech360 (Fiji) Limited shows several people running towards a vehicle and trying to pull the driver out.

The driver is then seen attempting to drive away, hitting another vehicle in the process.

The driver is then seen speeding towards the group of men who had tried to pull him out before hitting two police officers.

The impact throws both officers into the air.

Police confirm there were no fatalities, while investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Residents shaken after house fire in Bila, Nadi, investigations underway
item.description: A house fire in Bila, Nadi, today has left residents shaken, although no casualties have been reported. The National Fire Authority, with assistance from the Fiji Police Force, managed to contain the blaze and prevent the situation from becoming worse.
item.content:encoded:
A house fire in Bila, Nadi, today has left residents shaken, although no casualties have been reported.

The National Fire Authority, with assistance from the Fiji Police Force, managed to contain the blaze and prevent the situation from becoming worse.

The cause of the fire is still being investigated.

item.title: Lami youths celebrate Youth Day by bringing joy to Father Law Home residents
item.description: Youths from the Immaculate Conception Parish in Lami today celebrated Youth Day with residents of Father Law Home in Wailekutu. St Thomas Aquinas Catholic Church youth group member Joseph Balolo says a simple visit can mean a lot to those who may not always have family around to support them.
item.content:encoded:
Youths from the Immaculate Conception Parish in Lami today celebrated Youth Day with residents of Father Law Home in Wailekutu.

St Thomas Aquinas Catholic Church youth group member Joseph Balolo says a simple visit can mean a lot to those who may not always have family around to support them.

He says the visit was part of the youth group's annual programme , which includes four quarterly Masses held across the three churches under the parish and a final Mass at Father Law Home.

He says the visit was an opportunity for the youths to spend time with the elderly residents, engage in conversations and bring a little happiness into their day.

Balolo says the residents were equally happy to welcome them, making the experience meaningful for both the youths and the residents.

He is also encouraging young people to remain focused amid the challenges they face today, trust in God and, most importantly, listen to their parents.

The day concluded with the youths returning to the parish, where they shared lunch before enjoying an afternoon of netting and fellowship at a social gathering.
